# Why does removing the parade collision raise Water Street's forecast?

*Phase 3, 2026-10-14. Generated by `ml/experiments/single_event_case.py` (about 3 minutes, no
model fitting). Outputs: `single_event_sensitivity.json` (summary and probes),
`single_event_sensitivity_features.csv` (every feature before and after, with TreeSHAP), and
the optional extension `data/v2/extensions/segment_single_event_sensitivity_v2.csv` (top 1,000,
both rank definitions). Production files are unchanged.*

**Short answer.** Removing the 142-casualty collision raises the A57 Water Street forecast from
6.43 to 7.82 expected adjusted KSI casualties for 2026–27 (rank 10 → 2) because of three things:
- **Outside the learnt range.** The casualty and serious-injury counts it creates lie far beyond anything the model learnt from.
- **Spikes are discounted.** The model has learnt to treat severity spikes as partly noise. That is a regression-to-the-mean pattern.
- **Interactions carry the discount.** The discount acts through the features that did **not** change (junctions, nearby casualties), so the drop in the segment's own history is outweighed.

So the segment's place in the high-priority group does not depend on the event. Its forecast,
however, is sensitive to it, and in a non-monotone way.

## 1. The intervention, precisely

| Item | Definition |
|---|---|
| Model | the saved production LightGBM (`ml/outputs/explainability/production_lgbm.txt`); it reproduces the stored `blackspot_score` of the top 1,000 exactly (max difference 0.0). Nothing is refitted |
| Removed | each top-1,000 segment's single largest 2023–25 collision by adjusted KSI (ties broken by `collision_index`) |
| Recomputed | the segment's own 19 history features (`h_*`), with exactly the production feature code |
| Held fixed | all 21 road features and 5 context features, including crashes on nearby roads and elsewhere on the same stretch |
| Score units | expected DfT severity-adjusted KSI casualties on the segment, 2026 + 2027 total |
| Rank direction | 1 = highest forecast; a smaller number is a higher priority |
| Rank, one at a time | only this segment changes; every other segment keeps its production forecast |
| Rank, simultaneous | every top-1,000 segment loses its largest collision at once (the Phase-2 column `rank_without_largest_collision`) |

The script reproduces the Phase-2 result exactly (max difference 0.0 in forecasts; identical
simultaneous ranks).

## 2. Water Street (`A57-842C4722100B-00`)

**Its 2023–25 collisions.** The May 2025 parade collision had 142 casualties: 27 reported
serious, 43.8 serious/fatal after DfT's adjustment, none fatal. One other collision (2025) had
one serious casualty. Five were slight, each contributing 0.08–0.19 adjusted KSI (the adjustment
is a probability).

**What the removal changes** (`single_event_sensitivity_features.csv`):

| Feature | Before | After |
|---|---|---|
| Collisions (2023–25 / in 2025) | 7 / 3 | 6 / 2 |
| All casualties | 148 | 6 |
| Serious/fatal casualties, adjusted / reported | 45.5 / 28 | 1.6 / 1 |
| Serious/fatal casualties in 2025 (adjusted) | 45.0 | 1.1 |
| Serious/fatal collisions | 2 | 1 |
| Share of collisions that were serious/fatal | 0.29 | 0.17 |
| Shares at junctions / in darkness / wet / single-vehicle | 0.71 / 0.29 / 0.57 / 0.71 | 0.83 / 0.33 / 0.50 / 0.67 |
| Road and context (16 junctions, 143 adjusted KSI on nearby roads, 4.1 elsewhere on the stretch …) | unchanged | unchanged |

**Result.** Forecast 6.43 → **7.82** (+21.6%, +0.196 in log). Rank 10 → **2**, the same under
both rank definitions.

**TreeSHAP decomposition of the change** (log expected KSI; the family changes sum exactly to
+0.196):

| Feature family | Change in attribution | As a factor |
|---|---|---|
| All-casualty count | −0.217 | ×0.80 |
| Serious/fatal counts (7 features) | −0.109 | ×0.90 |
| Collision counts (4 features) | −0.084 | ×0.92 |
| Serious/fatal share | +0.029 | ×1.03 |
| Crash circumstances (6 shares and speed) | +0.077 | ×1.08 |
| **Road and context features, whose values did not change** | **+0.499** | **×1.65** |

The history features that changed lower the forecast in total (−0.30, ×0.74), as one would
expect. The rise comes from the **unchanged** features. Junctions gain +0.09, serious/fatal casualties on nearby roads +0.19, and the rest of the stretch +0.05. With the extreme counts present, the
trees route this segment through branches learnt from the few training segments with very large
casualty histories, and those branches give its other attributes less weight. Without the
extreme counts, its junction density and busy surroundings are credited as for any comparable
city-centre segment.

**One family at a time** (non-additive, so each family is substituted in both directions):

| Only this family changed | From "before" (6.43) | Restored in "after" (7.82) |
|---|---|---|
| All-casualty count | 5.88 (lower) | 7.60 (lower) |
| Serious/fatal counts | 6.79 (higher) | 6.56 (lower) |
| Collision counts | 6.76 (higher) | 7.28 (lower) |
| Serious/fatal share | 6.76 (higher) | 7.26 (lower) |
| Crash circumstances | 6.22 (lower) | 7.60 (lower) |

Read with care. These are probes of the model surface, and the mixed states never occur in data.
On its own, fewer casualties lowers the forecast (5.88). Fewer serious/fatal casualties, or a
lower serious/fatal share, raises it. The model rewards the casualty count and partly discounts the severity spike. For this
segment, even one fewer collision raises the forecast in isolation (6.76). Water Street is among
the 5.9% of top-1,000 segments where that happens (§4).

**Outside the learnt range.** The largest value on which the model ever splits is 62.5 for
all casualties, 6.06 for adjusted KSI, 11.5 for reported KSI and 4.06 for adjusted KSI in the latest
year. Water Street had 148, 45.5, 28 and 45.0. The model therefore cannot tell 148 casualties
from 63. Its response is whatever its highest-count leaves learnt. In the training feature window
(2021–23), the 304,292 collisions on scored segments included **one** collision with ≥ 20
casualties (maximum 70). The largest adjusted KSI from a single collision was 27.2.

## 3. What this demonstrates

| Concept | What the evidence shows |
|---|---|
| **Regression to the mean** | The model discounts isolated serious/fatal spikes: removing them raises the forecast, adding them can lower it. That matches the v2 finding that past KSI predicts future KSI worse than past collisions do. The top 500 by past KSI recorded only 50% of their past KSI in the next period. This is the pattern the model has learnt; the evidence does not prove that this particular segment would regress |
| **Correlated historical features** | One collision changes 14 of the 19 history features at once. Their individual SHAP values are near-duplicates (ρ ≥ 0.998 within the count group), so the change must be read by family, not by single feature |
| **Non-monotone LightGBM** | The production model has no monotone constraints. In isolation, more casualties raise the forecast, but more serious/fatal casualties, and in a few cases more collisions, can lower it. Monotone constraints are a candidate for a pre-registered v3 test. They are **not** applied here, and the production model is unchanged |
| **Sensitivity vs dependence** | **Sensitive:** the forecast moves by 22% and the rank by 8 places when one collision is removed. **Not dependent:** the segment stays in the high-priority group without it, and indeed rises. These are different properties. Neither makes the segment "independent of the event" |

**Which conclusion is supported for Water Street?**
- **Continued membership of a high-priority group: supported.** It is in the top 1,000 in all 20 spatial-bootstrap refits and remains near the top (rank 2) without the event.
- **Stability of the predicted burden: not supported.** The forecast changes by 22% when one record is removed, and the model's treatment of the event is extrapolation beyond its training range.
- **Stability of the numerical rank: not supported.** The rank is 10, 2 without the event, 5th–95th percentile #1–#687 across bootstrap refits, #1–#390 across history-window choices, and top-100 in only 60% of refits.

Keep the `single_event_flag`, show the rank range rather than the rank, and do not alter or drop
the score.

## 4. The rest of the top 1,000

| | Value |
|---|---|
| Forecast falls / rises / unchanged | 78.5% / 21.2% / 0.3% |
| Median change: fallers / risers | ×0.93 / ×1.04 (largest rise ×1.26, largest fall ×0.45) |
| Risers whose removed collision had exactly one serious casualty (adjusted KSI = 1.0) | 91% |
| Median rank change: one at a time / simultaneous | +47 / −1 |
| Leave the top 1,000: one at a time / simultaneous | 16.3% / 11.4% |
| Leave the top 5% (either definition) | 0 |
| Top-100 segments leaving the top 100 (one at a time) | 19 |

Rises are not confined to mass-casualty events. The largest relative rise (×1.26, A5038, rank
240) comes from removing a collision with a single serious casualty. Water Street's rise is the
third-largest. Among rising segments, the unchanged road and context features gain attribution
in 92% of cases. That is the same interaction mechanism as above, usually much smaller.

**Probes of the model surface** (top 1,000; one input changed, everything else fixed):

| Probe | Raises | Lowers |
|---|---|---|
| +5 adjusted KSI casualties (count and per-km value) | 86.8% | 8.5% |
| Serious/fatal share −0.1 | 63.0% | 25.9% |
| One fewer collision (count and per-km value) | 5.9% | 94.1% (lowers or unchanged) |

Phase 2 quoted 68% / 7% / 98% for the first and third probes from an interactive session whose
inputs were not recorded. These reproducible values replace them.

## 5. Consequences for the outputs

- `rank_without_largest_collision` in `segment_stability_v2.csv` is the **simultaneous** rank. It is left unchanged (it is an existing extension column) and documented as such in `data/v2/INTEGRATION_CONTRACT.md`.
- The new optional file `segment_single_event_sensitivity_v2.csv` carries both definitions, with the forecast before and after. A UI sentence about "this one collision" must use `rank_without_largest_collision_one_at_a_time`.
- The explained map now says "sensitive to / does not depend on" precisely instead of "does not depend on that collision".

## 6. Reproduce

```bash
.venv/Scripts/python ml/experiments/single_event_case.py     # ~3 min, ~4 GB, no fitting
```
